title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: The paper addresses efficient text classification, where deep neural models achieve strong accuracy but are slow to train and test. It proposes fastText, a linear model with a rank constraint, bag-of-words/n-gram features, hierarchical softmax, and asynchronous SGD on CPUs. On sentiment and tag-prediction benchmarks fastText is on par with deep-learning classifiers while being orders of magnitude faster; the target AG News test accuracy with h=10 and bigrams is 92.5%.

match_target.why: It directly matches the user's target hint (Table 1, AG News, fastText h=10 with bigrams), is the paper's central fastText sentiment result on a small, cheap dataset, and is much cheaper than the YFCC100M tag-prediction claim.

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

requirements.stmt: Represent each document as a normalized bag of features x_n over words and n-grams; the target configuration adds bigram features.
requirements.quote:
Instead, we use a bag of
n-grams as additional features to capture some par-
tial information about the local word order.

requirements.stmt: Model computes a hidden text representation by averaging embeddings of the document's features (lookup table A), then applies a linear classifier B and softmax.
requirements.quote:
The word representations are
then averaged into a text representation, which is in
turn fed to a linear classifier.

requirements.stmt: Train by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -1/N sum_n y_n log(f(BAx_n)).
requirements.quote:
this leads to minimizing the negative log-
likelihood over the classes:

requirements.stmt: Use hierarchical softmax with a Huffman coding tree during training and test, reducing complexity from O(kh) to O(h log2(k)).
requirements.quote:
based on the Huffman cod-
ing tree (Mikolov et al., 2013). During training, the
computational complexity drops to O(h log2(k)).

requirements.stmt: Train asynchronously on multiple CPUs using SGD with a linearly decaying learning rate.
requirements.quote:
This model is trained asynchronously on mul-
tiple CPUs using stochastic gradient descent and a
linearly decaying learning rate.

requirements.stmt: For sentiment analysis use 10 hidden units, run for 5 epochs, and select the learning rate on a validation set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}.
requirements.quote:
10 hidden units and run fastText for 5
epochs with a learning rate selected on a valida-
tion set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}.

requirements.stmt: Use the same hyperparameters across all sentiment datasets.
requirements.quote: FastText has been run with the same parameters for all the datasets.

requirements.stmt: Map n-grams with the hashing trick using the same hashing function as Mikolov et al. (2011); use 10M bins if only bigrams are used and 100M otherwise.
requirements.quote:

bins if we only used bigrams, and 100M otherwise.

data.name: YFCC100M tag-prediction dataset
data.how_to_get: The paper says a script recreating the filtered YFCC100M train/validation/test splits will be released; base YFCC100M is from Thomee et al. (2016).

stated_compute: Both char-CNN and VDCNN are trained on a NVIDIA Tesla K40 GPU, while our models are trained on a CPU using 20 threads. Training uses 20 threads for both models.
